{{short description|Reciprocity law for quadratic residue symbols of real quadratic number fields}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Scholz's reciprocity law''' is a [[reciprocity law]] for quadratic residue symbols of real [[quadratic number field]]s discovered by {{harvs|txt|first=Theodor |last=Schönemann|authorlink=Theodor Schönemann|year=1839}} and rediscovered by {{harvs|txt|first=Arnold|last=Scholz|authorlink=Arnold Scholz|year=1929}}.

==Statement==
Suppose that ''p'' and ''q'' are rational [[prime number|prime]]s congruent to 1 mod 4 such that the [[Legendre symbol]] (''p''/''q'') is 1. Then the ideal (''p'') factorizes in the [[ring of integers]] of '''Q'''({{radic|''q''}}) as (''p'')=𝖕𝖕' and similarly (''q'')=𝖖𝖖' in the ring of integers of '''Q'''({{radic|''p''}}).
Write ε<sub>''p''</sub> and ε<sub>''q''</sub> for the fundamental units in these quadratic fields. Then Scholz's reciprocity law says that
:[ε<sub>''p''</sub>/𝖖] = [ε<sub>''q''</sub>/𝖕] 
where [] is the quadratic residue symbol in a quadratic number field.
